5710.title: [skia-sync] Merge upstream chrome/m157 bug fixes
5710.body:
[M157] Integrate Vulkan sync and displacement precision fixes (#5710)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/449
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5714
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/d06aa926d8e17ccc2976658a9a18256a1c7f6629...ee5ff28274c8cd3f637f26cf9eed88a8cff1d96e

Bring the m157 GPU correctness fixes into release/4.157.x without changing
managed APIs, generated bindings, package or assembly versions, native ABI
version, or milestone identity.

~~ Propagate failed Vulkan fence waits through native submit ~~

Ganesh returned queue-submission success even when the subsequent
vkWaitForFences failed. Make GrVkPrimaryCommandBuffer::forceSync return
wait success and combine it with didSubmit for synchronous submission.
Keep the existing VK_TIMEOUT retry, device-loss handling, and command-pool
and semaphore cleanup; asynchronous submission does not gain a wait.

The existing managed GRContext.Submit remains void and discards the
C API boolean. This integrates the native correction, not a new managed
failure-reporting API.

~~ Match displacement sampling offsets to fp32 bounds ~~

Displacement calculated with fp16 could round differently from the fp32
bounds calculations, making the sampled position disagree with the
filter's computed bounds.

Use float2 for displacement scale and offset arithmetic in the runtime
effect and SkSL function, including both checked-in generated SkSL
strings. Channel samples and selectors remain half precision; the offset
calculation now uses fp32 before adding to the sampling coordinate,
matching the existing SkV2 scale upload.

~~ Record landed native ancestry without changing reviewed content ~~

Update externals/skia and its Component Governance registration to
ee5ff28274c8cd3f637f26cf9eed88a8cff1d96e. Record upstream chrome/m157
at 784c6a80e286e0f5b541e6606bba261ba3e8d2b6 while retaining milestone 157.

The native merge directly contains reviewed head
781384f7db300dc9255dc38cfc11d584a587ee17 and has the identical tree,
fc96fe4984172f9c889d31722b9354958a19139d. The dependent repin updates
only the gitlink and matching manifest SHA, preserving the reviewed
native source while recording the actual landed merge ancestry.

C API declarations and native DEPS remain unchanged. Independent binding
regeneration matched the reviewed outputs, so no wrapper or generated
declaration changes are needed. Tree equality preserves that source
evidence; it does not prove execution of Vulkan device-loss paths or
rounding-sensitive rendering cases on physical GPUs.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

5688.title: [M157] Integrate Ganesh rendering and Graphite clip fixes
5688.body:
[M157] Integrate Ganesh rendering and Graphite clip fixes (#5688)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/445
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5699
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/24c21cc82f1f03e03740b742309c7a5e0d50beb3...d06aa926d8e17ccc2976658a9a18256a1c7f6629

Bring the m157 GPU correctness fixes into release/4.157.x without changing
managed APIs, generated bindings or the servicing line's version identities.

~~ Avoid stale atlas work after empty Ganesh flushes ~~

Empty flushes could leave per-flush token comparisons stale. Advance
the draw token when GrOpFlushState resets and catch the flush token up,
so work scheduled during one flush is not treated as pending later.

~~ Correct transformed ellipse and rounded-rectangle geometry ~~

Off-diagonal matrix coefficients were mixed between rows when mapping
rrect radii and ellipse/rrect stroke widths. Correct those transforms
and remove the redundant quarter-turn swap: the corrected mapping
already produces device-space axes.

Clamp corner radii to half the transformed bounds to prevent overlap.
Document the rect-preserving and similarity assumptions behind the
mapping shortcuts.

~~ Keep Graphite clip draws within pass capacity ~~

Flush checks omitted clip elements that still needed recording. Count
them without counting already-recorded DrawListLayer clips twice.
Because a flush resets clips to undrawn, a fresh pass must fit the draw
and its full effective clip stack. Warn and skip a draw that cannot fit
rather than exceeding render-step capacity. Allow capacity assertions
to accept a pass exactly at its limit.

DeviceTestClipRenderStepLimits exercises accumulating and reused clip
stacks, an oversized stack, and a normal draw after restoring it,
asserting that a recording can still be made.

~~ Record landed native ancestry without changing reviewed content ~~

Update externals/skia and its Component Governance registration to
d06aa926d8e17ccc2976658a9a18256a1c7f6629. Record upstream chrome/m157
at fef60e46c522b87e5802ddf0a215a763dd5e0483 while retaining milestone 157.

The native merge directly contains reviewed head
87950a45740362dbb4f5bff22e25a05f0f8936d1 and has the identical tree,
3df572a4f085f94771a95608850bb21792bfa6bb. The dependent repin updates
only the gitlink and matching manifest SHA, not the reviewed native source.

C API declarations and native DEPS remain unchanged. Independent binding
regeneration matched the committed outputs, so no wrapper or generated
declaration changes are needed.

5670.title: [M157] Sync upstream Skia chrome/m157 bug fixes
5670.body:
[M157] Sync upstream Skia chrome/m157 bug fixes (#5670)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/440
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5674
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/cd151a3c30953e87a673d9840ad1e525667b46ee...24c21cc82f1f03e03740b742309c7a5e0d50beb3

Bring the m157 rendering and Vulkan fixes into release/4.157.x without
changing managed APIs, generated bindings, or package versions.

~~ Correct reflected hairline square caps ~~

Negative-determinant transforms incorrectly took a unit local-space
fallback when constructing square caps on zero-length hairlines,
allowing scaling to enlarge them arbitrarily. Use the signed inverse
determinant for the half-pixel outset and suppress non-finite results.

~~ Stabilize text atlas selection ~~

Ganesh's flat-interpolation hint does not guarantee integral atlas
indices. Round the interpolated index before converting to int in
ordinary and LCD texture selection to avoid sampling the wrong atlas.

~~ Respect affected Mali device-loss cleanup timing ~~

Ganesh and Graphite delay affected device-loss cleanup paths by 1 ms
for ARM proprietary Vulkan driver versions >=42 and <56. These drivers
can return from waits before device destruction is safe.

~~ Record landed native ancestry without changing reviewed content ~~

Update externals/skia and its Component Governance registration to
24c21cc82f1f03e03740b742309c7a5e0d50beb3. Record upstream chrome/m157
at 851b8fee76806e84c668d40bdaf17a6468e1ce6f.

The native merge directly contains reviewed head

5565.title: Fix generated LibraryImport calling conventions
5565.body:
Fix generated LibraryImport calling conventions (#5565)

Fixes: #5168

Generate `UnmanagedCallConv` metadata with `CallConvCdecl` for every
`USE_LIBRARY_IMPORT` declaration. This makes generated `LibraryImport`
declarations use the same cdecl convention as the existing `DllImport` and
delegate paths, without changing the public API or native exports.

The missing convention can select a different ABI on Windows x86; #5168
reported stack growth in optimized, inlined managed calls to cdecl native
exports. Regenerate the SkiaSharp, HarfBuzzSharp, SceneGraph, Skottie, and
Resources bindings so their `LibraryImport` declarations carry the explicit
metadata.

Add `LibraryImportsUseCdeclCallingConvention`, which reflects each of the
five interop API types and requires every `LibraryImport` method to have
exactly `CallConvCdecl` metadata. This validates the compiled attribute
independently of a Windows x86 release workload.

The PR check runs completed successfully. Windows x86 runtime validation of
the reported stack-growth symptom remains outstanding.

Co-authored-by: mattleibow <1096616+mattleibow@users.noreply.github.com>

5599.title: Use authoritative native SONAMEs and tighten Skia sync checks
5599.body:
Use authoritative native SONAMEs and tighten Skia sync checks (#5599)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5597
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/41814571700
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/41835505198

Derive artifact expectations from their existing source of truth and
require dependency evidence before accepting upstream pins. Keep the
existing sync phases and validation gates rather than introducing another
version inventory or dependency-management mechanism.

~~ Read artifact SONAMEs from the authoritative version file ~~

The original m158 sync advanced scripts/VERSIONS.txt to Skia SONAME
158.0.0 while Get-NativeArtifactInventory still expected 157.0.0. Maintaining
a second literal map made otherwise valid milestone updates leave stale
Linux alias expectations.

Copy scripts/VERSIONS.txt beside the native test host's Cases directory
and read the libSkiaSharp and HarfBuzz SONAME entries from that fixed path.
Require one numeric three-component match per library and fail when the
input is missing or the matching entries are absent or duplicated.

Continue constructing exact expected alias paths; do not discover versions
from the artifacts being tested, add wildcard expectations, or weaken
inventory coverage. HarfBuzz uses its own SONAME entry rather than following
the Skia milestone.

The native test host built on macOS, and PowerShell inventory checks
verified current aliases, an m158 transition, unchanged HarfBuzz, and
missing, malformed and duplicate inputs. The full native-artifact matrix
was not exercised by these checks.

~~ Compare dependency versions before accepting upstream pins ~~

The baseline sync initially selected older upstream pins for Brotli,
Expat, FreeType, HarfBuzz, libjpeg-turbo, libpng, libwebp and zlib.
The independent review missed the downgrades; the agent corrected them
after dependency hydration exposed missing manifest version evidence.

Require the research phase to record source-backed semantic versions at
both exact dependency revisions before accept-target decisions, independent
review or merged-dependency hydration. Compare using the dependency's own
version scheme. Preserve a newer fork pin unless a reviewed compatibility
requirement justifies the downgrade and accounts for lost fork/security
fixes; missing evidence blocks acceptance.

Make the reviewer explicitly check those comparisons and unexplained
downgrades. Retain the existing manifest gate as a backstop, and retain
compatibility rolls when target source actually requires a newer API.

The fresh m158 run preserved the eight newer fork pins upfront and passed
the version helper on its first invocation. Source inspection also showed
that retained Vulkan-Headers 1.4.365 already contained the required m158
structs, avoiding the baseline's unnecessary 1.4.366 roll.

~~ Make helper examples work with staged skills and local runs ~~

Automation stages the skill outside the mutable product checkout, so a
helper's own location cannot reliably identify the product repository.
Supply --repo-root in the native-build examples and --skia-root in both
fork-audit examples. The latter is the audit helper's supported flag,
rather than the --repo-root argument mistakenly used in the baseline run.

Provide the complete local update_versions.py invocation, including exact
base and upstream identities. Its automation path consumes SKIA_SYNC_*
values directly, but local execution requires explicit arguments; document
that distinction when rerunning final metadata reconciliation.

Clarify that shim filenames come from the fork's src/c and include/c
directories, not upstream, and that expected search no-matches or absent
optional paths must be handled without swallowing tool errors.

The existing helper suite passed 51 tests. Live validation at fixes commit
0bcee2dee067031106cf19618bc5566d92aff8a7 completed the Linux x64 native
source build, binding regeneration, managed build and unfiltered console
suite, publishing SkiaSharp #5600 and mono/skia#427. This was not full
native-artifact matrix coverage or proof that exploration mistakes were
eliminated; upstream also advanced between runs, so timing differences
are not a controlled efficiency result.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
